title: Taiwan Can’t Fight Beijing’s History War While Erasing Its Own ROC Legacy
author: Ivan I-Wei Huang
text:
Credit: Jack Hong / Shutterstock
At last week’s summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and China’s President Xi Jinping, the White House described the United States and China as World War II allies who “fought side by side to win the war.” It was a small phrase with a large omission. The government that represented China during the war, and fought alongside the United States against Japan, was the Republic of China (ROC). The government Xi leads – the People’s Republic of China (PRC) – did not exist until 1949, four years after Japan’s surrender. By collapsing the two into a single, unbroken “China,” the summit’s language risked allowing the PRC to inherit the legacy of a war it did not fight.Taiwan’s government noticed. Its Mainland Affairs Council pushed back, insisting that the ROC was the “true ally” that fought with the United States during the war, and emphasizing that the PRC did not even exist during World War II. Deputy Foreign Minister Wu Chih-chung went further, calling the framing an act of “de-ROC-ization” – in which the Republic of China’s very existence is being erased from history, and replaced by the Chinese Communist Party. “We should feel very distressed,” Wu added. [...]
